title: UGC Ads on Facebook: How Much to Make and Run Them in 2026
summary: UGC ads on Facebook cost more than the video. See what creator, AI and managed production cost, what Meta's budget rules add, and how a first month adds up.
body_markdown:
A Facebook UGC program has three cost lines: the videos, the rights to run them, and the media you pay Meta to deliver them. In 2025 and 2026 marketplace data, one short creator video costs about $100 to $200 before extras, a managed package works out to $375 a video, and the media budget is a separate number you choose. If you want finished UGC-style ads without managing creators, we recommend[Knowlify](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) , a done-for-you AI UGC service priced by custom quote.


Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared. Published prices are checked as of October 2026, the arithmetic is ours, and none of it is a quote for your brief. For a wider comparison of creator marketplaces, see[how much UGC costs](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-much-does-ugc-cost) .


## What does a Facebook UGC video cost to make?


Four published sources give a workable range. They measure different things, so read the last column before you compare the numbers.


Route Published figure What it measures or includes


[Knowlify](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) , our recommendation Custom quote, not published Finished AI UGC-style ads with AI presenters, each checked by a person before delivery


[Collabstr 2026 report](https://collabstr.com/2026-influencer-marketing-report) $180 average asking price; $154 average paid UGC price per engagement, from 2025 data on more than 21,000 collaborations


[Pitchlo UGC Pay Report](https://www.pitchlo.com/ugc-creator-earnings) $100 median per video; half between $50 and $200 Budgets advertised in more than 640 per-video briefs, December 2025 to October 2026


[Billo](https://billo.app/blog/how-billo-pricing-works/) Videos from $99 each; managed service from $2,000 a month Creator pay, two revisions and usage rights on a platform video


[Brighter Click](https://www.brighterclick.com/ugc-agency) $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators Edited videos in 9:16 and 4:5 with unlimited usage rights; 10 to 14 business days listed for the package


Collabstr shows what creators asked and what brands paid. Pitchlo shows what brands advertised, a budget rather than a settled invoice. Neither source says it includes a paid-ad license, product shipping or your own editing time, so treat both as the price of the creator's work.


The $99 and $375 figures differ for a reason. A platform sells a creator's video, while a managed package also sells sourcing, briefing and editing. Brighter Click's package divides to $375 a video by our arithmetic, and the two prices buy different amounts of work.


## Which add-ons raise a Facebook UGC bill?


The base rate rarely covers the ad you run. Four add-ons matter most on Facebook.


- **Paid-ad access to the creator's handle.**[Meta's help center](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/442108830566254) says running an ad from a creator's handle requires permission from that partner, and the partner can withdraw it. A withdrawn permission can interrupt a live test, so ask how long the permission lasts.
- **A whitelisting or Spark Ads license.** An[Insense pricing cheatsheet from 2024](https://lp.insense.pro/hubfs/How%20to%20Compensate%20Creators.pdf) lists starting prices of $100 to $150 a month for a 30-day Meta whitelisting or Spark Ads license. Brighter Click says it can set up whitelisting, also called partnership ads or creator licensing, but its page does not price that separately, so ask whether it is included.
- **Raw footage.** The same cheatsheet suggests $50 to $100 or more for raw files, which your editor needs to cut new versions.
- **Usage rights.** Billo says an approved video can be used in ads and on your own channels, and Brighter Click lists unlimited usage rights. Confirm what "usage" covers before you assume another provider includes paid ads on every channel.


An AI presenter has no handle to license, so the first two lines do not apply to AI UGC. The trade-off is that it cannot run as a partnership ad from a real creator's account.


## What does running the ads on Facebook cost?


Media spend pays Meta for delivery, and no creative price includes it. You choose the budget, but[Meta's minimum budgets](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448) vary by country and objective, and Ads Manager shows an alert when a budget is too low. The same help page says that with a cost-per-result goal, your daily budget should be at least five times that goal.


A management fee is a third line if someone else runs the account.[Adside AI](https://www.adside.ai/pricing) is one published example: 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum, covering strategy, creative production, launch, optimization and reporting. Our[Facebook ad agency pricing guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ad-agency-pricing) compares more fee structures, and[how much Facebook ads cost](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-much-do-facebook-ads-cost) covers cost-per-click and CPM benchmarks.


## What does a first month of Facebook UGC testing cost?


The table totals one illustrative month. The $20 goal, the 8 hours and the $60 rate are assumptions, not market data, so replace them with your own.


Line Amount Basis


8 platform videos $792 Billo's $99 starting price


Your team's time $480 Assumed 8 hours at $60 an hour


Meta media, 30 days $3,000 Assumed $20 goal, so $100 a day under Meta's five-times guidance


Self-run total $4,272 Production is about 30% of this


Management fee, if outsourced $3,500 Adside AI's minimum, because 10% of $3,000 is only $300


Total with an agency running media $7,772


Two things stand out. For a small test, media is the largest line, so a cheap video does not make a cheap program. And a fee floor can exceed the media it manages, which is why you should price an agency at your real spend. To compare providers fairly, divide each route's total by the ads you can actually run, using the formula in our[UGC cost guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-much-does-ugc-cost) .
